title: Complete Prime Number
summary: Given an integer num, determine if every prefix and every suffix of num is a prime number.
statement: Given an integer num, determine if every prefix and every suffix of num is a prime number. Single-digit numbers are considered prime and are also considered complete. Return true if all prefixes and suffixes are prime, otherwise return false.
constraints: num is between one and one billion.
Every nonempty decimal prefix and every nonempty decimal suffix must be prime.
Single-digit inputs qualify exactly when that digit is prime.
hints: The number has only logarithmically many prefixes and suffixes.
Generate each decimal slice and test primality by trial division through its integer square root.
Return false on the first composite slice and true only after every length passes both sides.
The enumeration is exactly the definition, while trial division is a complete primality test for these bounded values.
editorial: The enumeration is exactly the definition, while trial division is a complete primality test for these bounded values.

tests.explanation: Prefixes 2 and 23 and suffixes 3 and 23 are all prime.
The full value 39 and suffix nine are composite, so it fails.
